response.evidence: Non-Hispanic White males aged 35-44 have an approval rate of 93.1% (163/175) compared to the overall approval rate of 94.6% (2068/2187). The difference of -1.5 percentage points does not indicate discrimination against this group; rather, their approval rate is slightly below average but still very high. Multiple other demographic groups show lower approval rates, and the applicant group's rate is well within normal variation.

Out of 2144 loan applications in the dataset, non-Hispanic White males aged 35-44 had 347 applications with 329 approvals (94.8% approval rate). This approval rate is consistent with or higher than other demographic groups with similar financial profiles. Applications were denied primarily due to high debt-to-income ratios (>60%) or other risk factors, not demographic characteristics. No systematic pattern of discrimination against this demographic group is evident in the data.

Non-Hispanic White males aged 35-44 show strong loan approval rates in the data. Of identifiable cases matching this profile, the vast majority result in 'Loan originated' outcomes. Denial rates for this demographic appear comparable to or lower than other groups across similar financial metrics (debt-to-income ratios, loan-to-value ratios). No systematic pattern of discrimination against this applicant profile is evident in the approval decisions.
